# Regression essentials {.unnumbered}

Six weeks revise the regression ideas that SEM is built on. Before you start, try the [readiness checklist](readiness.qmd) as a quick self-test: if you can already do everything for a week, skim that week and do only its task.

| Week | Topic | Why it matters later |
|:--|:--|:--|
| [R1](r1-covariance.qmd) | Covariance and simple regression | A slope is built from variances and covariances |
| [R2](r2-multiple.qmd) | Multiple regression | What "holding the other predictors constant" means |
| [R3](r3-inference.qmd) | Inference and model comparison | Testing whether a set of extra predictors improves a model |
| [R4](r4-assumptions.qmd) | Assumptions and diagnostics | Checking residuals, outliers and influential cases |
| [R5](r5-moderation.qmd) | Moderation and categorical predictors | Whether an effect depends on another variable or differs between groups |
| [R6](r6-mediation.qmd) | Mediation and causal thinking | Indirect effects, the bootstrap, and what a model can and cannot show about causes |

The block ends with a [readiness checklist](readiness.qmd). After it, [Week 0](../sem/week-00.qmd) of the SEM block refits these same regressions in Amos.

Every week also draws its model as a **path diagram**, the way Amos draws models: rectangles for measured variables, circles for error terms, single-headed arrows for regression paths and curved two-headed arrows for correlations. [R1](r1-covariance.qmd) explains the conventions. By the time you reach SEM, the diagrams will already be familiar.

Use one practice dataset for all six weeks, so you are learning ideas rather than new variables each time. The [Student Life Survey](../course/dataset.qmd) is designed for this.
